alalal-c48331-d1e104.summary: Rubric of Article 21: whether God is within all things without being enclosed and outside all without being excluded, and how God is called new and old.

alalal-c48331-d1e117.summary: Introduces the question on Lombard's (Augustine's) statement that God is more interior than every thing, since all things are in him.

alalal-c48331-d1e129.summary: Notes that the saying 'within, not enclosed; outside, not excluded' comes from this text, and objects that being simultaneously within and not enclosed seems impossible.
concepts: intra non inclusus, extra non exclusus

alalal-c48331-d1e143.summary: Reply: this is said because God does not follow the laws of place and is not in place as located, but by the presence of his substance giving all things being, power and operation. Since there is nothing outside which there is not something else, he is never within in a way that excludes being outside.
claims: God is within and outside all things at once because he is present by causal substance, not as located.

alalal-c48331-d1e163.summary: 'Older' signifies the duration of eternity; 'newer' signifies the novelty of his effects and influences, since God in himself is not new, being without recent beginning, as Scripture and earlier discussion state. Or he may be called new because of the ever-fresh vigour of his power, which he has from eternity.
claims: God is called old by his eternity and new by the novelty of his effects or the freshness of his power, not by any beginning.

alalal-c48331.summary: Article 21 explains the formula that God is within all things without being enclosed and outside all without being excluded, and how God is called both new and old. Because God does not follow the laws of place but is present by his substance giving being, power and operation, his being within never excludes his being outside. He is 'older' by the duration of eternity and 'newer' by the novelty of his effects or the ever-fresh vigour of his eternal power, never by any recent beginning.
claims: God is within all things without enclosure and outside without exclusion because his presence is causal, not locative.
God is called old by eternity and new by his effects or ever-fresh power, never by a beginning.
